stories.title: Iran ties Hormuz reopening to US concessions on demands
stories.summary: Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman defining new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz but repeated that the US must meet other conditions, including compensation and an end to sanctions and military threats, before the strategic waterway is reopened. A US official told journalists on Friday that Iran and Oman were close to a deal that could pave the way for restoring safe passage through the strait, a major conduit for oil and gas shipping before Iran blocked Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks on Tehran that began in late February. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said an agreement with Oman on the strait was in its "final stages" but reiterated comments made on Saturday that Tehran would not reopen the channel unless the US met certain demands made by Tehran. The deal with Iran would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the US fulfills those conditions and the strait is reopened, Iran's Mehr news agency quoted him as saying.

stories.summary: A Dublin sailor has been inspired by his dad's battle with Parkinson’s disease to undertake a solo, non-stop, unassisted race around the world to raise money for charity. Karl Smith will become the first Irish person to complete the Global Solo Challenge if he is successful. He has set himself a goal of raising €1 million for Parkinson’s charities by taking part in the challenge. "It's one of the most challenging things you can do in sailing and when you're at sea for four to five months, the outcome is uncertain for everyone."

stories.title: Taoiseach defends Government jet amid navigation concern
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin has reiterated the Coalition's defence of the new Government jet but stopped short of denying reports it may have difficulty landing in fog due to the absence of an Israel-made navigational system. The Journal.ie reported this week how the €53 million aircraft was purchased from a French firm without a FalconEye system, which normally sits on the plane's nose and helps it land in fog or other weather conditions that limit visibility, as it was made by an Israeli manufacturer. The Government adopted a policy in 2024 of not awarding Israeli companies defence contracts owing to an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice against Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Speaking as he visited Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann in Belfast, Mr Martin insisted the jet "has been very effective".

stories.title: Consumer spending up 5% in July: AIB Spend Trend
stories.summary: Consumer spending rose by 5% last month, according to AIB, as hot weather benefitted hotels, restaurants and amusement parks. The bank's latest Spend Trend report - which analysed 81.4 million card transactions by AIB customers in the month - recorded a 5% increase in overall spend, with in-store spending up by the same percentage. Online spending by the bank's customers fell by 1% in July, though. The report said spending on accommodation rose by 9% year-on-year, while restaurant and dining spend was up 8%.

stories.title: Iran issues demands for reopening of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran set preconditions for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including compensation for war damages, complicating a potential deal to open the waterway essential to the world economy. It has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel struck Iran in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage, attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route. Continued attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire. Mediators have since urged both sides to return to the terms of a June memorandum.

stories.title: Camogie final preview: Best of the era battling for title
stories.summary: For the third year in a row, and the fourth time this decade, Galway and Cork are battling it out to land the biggest prize in camogie, the O'Duffy Cup. The Tribe County come into this afternoon's showpiece as defending champions having halted the Rebels' three-in-a-row bid last summer thanks to Carrie Dolan's winner at the death. They'll be looking to complete the senior double for the county after the footballers' triumph over Kerry last weekend. Cork were the last county to do so back in 2015. This will be Galway's 23rd appearance in an All-Ireland final, with five titles in that time. They had their breakthrough in 1996, but the Connacht women had to wait until 2013 for a second title, adding a further three to their total since 2019.

The allegations intensify the position of Infantino, who worked at UEFA for 16 years and was its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his aborted plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

stories.title: Carney: Irish fans will embrace 'relentless' rugby league
stories.summary: Former rugby league star Brian Carney is confident the Irish sporting public will embrace next year's historic Super League fixtures at the RDS. Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors will face off at the newly redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday 24 April 2027, with St Helens taking on Hull FC at the same venue the next day. It is not an unprecedented move. While it will be the first time Super League games have been held in this country, Warrington and Wigan previously met at Shelbourne Park back in 1934, while Wigan returned to the capital in 1995 to face Leeds in a Charity Shield fixture. Corkman Carney forged a highly distinguished career in rugby league, lining out for Hull, Wigan Warriors, Newcastle Knights (in Australia) and Warrington Wolves. He also represented Munster in rugby union, won four caps for Ireland and played international rugby sevens.

stories.title: Armagh Observatory to host special event for solar eclipse
stories.summary: On Wednesday, 12 August, the moon will cover approximately 94% of the sun, causing a partial solar eclipse. It will be the deepest eclipse seen from the UK and Ireland since the total eclipse of August 1999, and the last time that such an eclipse will be seen here until 2090. A total solar eclipse will cover a narrow path of our planet, likely crossing Greenland, Iceland, northern Spain, and a small portion of Portugal. Although Ireland won't see a total eclipse, the 94% partial eclipse has been eagerly awaited by professionals in the field for decades.

stories.title: Money talcs: Why J&J offered $5.5bn to end cancer cases
stories.summary: Allegations that some of Johnson & Johnson’s talc-based products – including their iconic baby powder – were to blame for customers developing cancer have been around for many years now. The first cases date back to 2009, and despite multiple attempts by the company to shut the controversy down – and despite numerous adjudications and settlements – it has continued to rumble on. The claims centre largely on allegations that the talc products caused either ovarian cancer or mesothelioma - a rare form of cancer that affects the membrane around internal organs. That cancer has traditionally tended to afflict people who worked in mines, or in industries that used a lot of asbestos, before the risks of that material were known.

stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned, during a visit to Belgrade, that Ukraine was facing a winter with basically no working thermal power plants as overnight Russian strikes left four dead, including a child, in the Kyiv region. Speaking alongside his Serbian counterpart, Aleksandar Vucic, the Ukrainian leader said Russia's latest overnight attacks and shelling of frontline communities combined had killed 13 people in the last 24 hours. "Russian missiles are aimed precisely at making the lives of Ukrainians unbearable," Mr Zelensky told reporters during his first official visit to Belgrade, highlighting that the attacks often target Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Ukraine was left with "virtually no intact thermal power plants" as it braced for the upcoming heating season, Mr Zelensky said.

stories.summary: Ailish O'Reilly certainly made no bones about it, in the minutes after skipper Carrie Dolan lofted the winner from a placed ball to give Galway their fifth Glen Dimplex All-Ireland senior title 12 months ago, and then received the O’Duffy Cup. In the build-up, Cork had tried all they could to deflect talk of the three in-a-row but you cannot control external narratives. Nor can you control how the opposition use them. "All we heard all week was 'the three-in-a-row, the three-in-a-row’… It suited us down to the ground. All the talk was about Cork. It felt like we were just coming up to show up and they were just going to be handed the trophy," O’Reilly stated indignantly. "We kept it in ourselves the last week but we were so riled up to be honest."

stories.summary: TV presenter Fearne Cotton has reflected on becoming "sort of a hermit" two years ago when she felt "debilitated" and "crippled with anxiety" during a time of personal challenges. The broadcaster and podcaster, 44, revealed she needed surgery to remove two benign tumours from her jaw in December 2024. A week later it was announced she had separated from husband Jesse Wood, the son of Rolling Stones guitarist Ronnie Wood, after 10 years of marriage. In an interview with The Sun on Sunday, the mother-of-two opened up about being "stuck in deep anxiety" during this turbulent time in her life.

stories.title: Irish buyers are choosing EVs, but concerns remain
stories.summary: When faced with the big decision of buying a new car, more Irish consumers are choosing to go fully electric. For the first time, battery electric cars have become the most popular new private vehicle, taking the title from hybrids. "It's the future coming," said independent motoring expert at Carzone, Conor Faughnan. The latest figures from the Society of the Irish Motor Industry (SIMI) show that among all new car registrations in July - a proxy for sales - battery electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for 26% of the market.

stories.title: Former Labour TD Michael Conaghan dies aged 81
stories.summary: Former Labour Party TD and Lord Mayor of Dublin Michael Conaghan has died at the age of 81. Mr Conaghan was elected to the Dáil for Dublin South Central in 2011, serving one term before stepping away prior to the 2016 General Election. The Donegal native took the second of two Labour seats in the constituency alongside Eric Byrne on a memorable day for the party at the 2011 election. He served 20 years as a councillor on Dublin City Council after his election in 1991, topping the poll on three occasions in the Ballyfermot ward.

stories.title: Targeting goals pays off for Cork in revenge mission
stories.summary: Cork manager Ger Manley admitted his side were going after goals as they reclaimed the All-Ireland camogie title with a one-point victory over Galway at Croke Park. The Rebels' two second-half goals were the only majors the Tribeswomen conceded over the course of the entire championship, and they were crucial in turning the final around on Jones' Road. Saoirse McCarthy and Orlaith Cahalane delivered the crucial scores as Cork came from two down at the break to lead by six with the game in its closing stages. Galway would hit the next five points but goalkeeper Sarah Healy's shot with the last puck of the game cleared the crossbar when a goal would have won it for them.
